text:
In the arrangement shown in figure $a_{1}, a_{2}, a_{3}$ and $a_{4}$ are the accelerations of masses $m_{1}, m_{2}, m_{3}$ and $m_{4}$ respectively. Which of the following relation is true for this arrangement?


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Take all accelerations positive downward, and let $a_{P_{2}}$ and $a_{P_{3}}$ be the accelerations of the two movable pulleys. Each string has constant length.

String over the fixed pulley (holding $m_{1}$ and pulley $P_{2}$): $a_{1}+a_{P_{2}}=0\Rightarrow a_{P_{2}}=-a_{1}$.

String over $P_{2}$ (holding $m_{2}$ and pulley $P_{3}$), with lengths measured from $P_{2}$: $(a_{2}-a_{P_{2}})+(a_{P_{3}}-a_{P_{2}})=0\Rightarrow a_{P_{3}}=2a_{P_{2}}-a_{2}=-2a_{1}-a_{2}$.

String over $P_{3}$ (holding $m_{3}$ and $m_{4}$): $(a_{3}-a_{P_{3}})+(a_{4}-a_{P_{3}})=0\Rightarrow a_{3}+a_{4}=2a_{P_{3}}=-4a_{1}-2a_{2}$.

$4a_{1}+2a_{2}+a_{3}+a_{4}=0$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Evening Shift

text:
Given below are two statements : One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.

Assertion A : If we move from poles to equator, the direction of acceleration due to gravity of earth always points towards the center of earth without any variation in its magnitude.

Reason R : At equator, the direction of acceleration due to the gravity is towards the center of earth.

In the light of above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Assertion A is false. While the direction of acceleration due to gravity does always point towards the center of the Earth, its magnitude actually varies from the poles to the equator. This is due to the Earth's rotation and the fact that Earth is not a perfect sphere but an oblate spheroid, meaning it's slightly flattened at the poles and bulging at the equator.

Reason R is true. At the equator, the direction of acceleration due to gravity is towards the center of the Earth.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Evening Shift

text: If $ρ$ is the density and $η$ is coefficient of viscosity of fluid which flows with a speed v in the pipe of diameter d, the correct formula for Reynolds number $R_{e}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The Reynolds number (Re) is a dimensionless quantity used in fluid mechanics to predict the onset of turbulence. It is defined as:

$Re=\frac{ρvd}{η}$

where:

$ρ$ is the fluid density
$v$ is the fluid velocity
$d$ is a characteristic linear dimension (for a pipe, this is typically the diameter)
$η$ is the dynamic viscosity of the fluid

So, Option C is the correct answer:

$R_{e}=\frac{ρvd}{η}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Evening Shift

text: Sixty four conducting drops each of radius 0.02 m and each carrying a charge of 5 $μ$C are combined to form a bigger drop. The ratio of surface charge density of bigger drop to the smaller drop will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Surface charge density of a spherical conductor is given by,

$σ=\frac{q}{4πr^{2}}$

When all smaller drops combine, the radius of the bigger drop is given by 

$\frac{4}{3}πR^{3}=64\left (\frac{4}{3}πr^{3}\right )$

$\begin{array}{ll} \mathrm{R}^{3} & =64r^{3} \\  \\ \mathrm{R} & =4r \\  \\ σ^{'} & =\dfrac{64q}{4π(4r)^{2}}=4σ \end{array}$

$\text{Hence,}\frac{σ^{'}}{σ}=4:1$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Evening Shift

text: A ball is projected vertically upward with an initial velocity of $50 ms^{-1}$ at t = 0s. At t = 2s, another ball is projected vertically upward with same velocity. At $t = __________ s$, second ball will meet the first ball $(g = 10 ms^{-2})$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
At $t = 2 s, v_{1} = 50$ $-$ 2 $\times$ 10 = 30 m/s

$v_{2} = 50 m/s$

$\therefore$ $a_{$rel} = g $-$ g = 0

$S=\frac{u^{2}-v^{2}}{2g}=\frac{50^{2}-30^{2}}{2\times 10}=\frac{1600}{20}=80$ m

$\therefore$ $v_{$rel} = 50 $-$ 30 = 20 m/s

$\therefore$ $\Delta t=\frac{80}{20}=4s$

$\therefore$ required time t = 2 + 4 = 6 s
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Evening Shift

text: A travelling microscope is used to determine the refractive index of a glass slab. If 40 divisions are there in 1 cm on main scale and 50 Vernier scale divisions are equal to 49 main scale divisions, then least count of the travelling microscope is $__________$ $\times$ $10^{-6} m$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
40 M = 1 cm

$\Rightarrow$ M = 0.025 cm .......... (1)

Also, 50 V = 49 M

$\Rightarrow$ Least count = M $-$ V = M $-$ $\frac{49}{50}$ M = $\frac{M}{50}$

$\Rightarrow$ LC = $\frac{0.025}{50}$ cm

= $\frac{250}{50}$ $\times$ $10^{-6} m$

$\Rightarrow$ LC = 5 $\times$ $10^{-6} m$
